note: HAND-CURATED from live-verified sources. Every url returned HTTP 200 on lastVerified date via browser UA (stlouiscountymo.gov blocks scrapers and was confirmed in a real browser instead). This is the fastest-rotting data in the app - re-verify before trusting. Dead or hijacked as of 2026-08-19 and deliberately EXCLUDED: ncsurvivorsunion.org (domain lapsed, now redirects to an unrelated commercial site), tennesseeharmreduction.com (host suspended), urbansurvivorsunion.org (empty), hrcsd.org (404 at every path tried), testri.org, dancesafe.org/chapters (404). Also EXCLUDED as unconfirmed - the service is reported in news, a job posting or a third-party directory but the organization's own pages do not mention it: Project Weber/RENEW spectrometer (RI), Access Point Denver (CO), Compassionate Addiction Treatment (WA), Southside Harm Reduction (MN), Roanoke/VHRC (VA).
reality: Most US drug checking lives inside syringe service programs, so the practical route is usually a local one - the list below now covers around twenty states. Sending a sample yourself is possible in a few places: Transparency Testing takes samples from anyone by post for a fee, and PA Groundhogs posts free kits anywhere in Pennsylvania. DrugsData paused intake in April 2024 and expects no change before 2027; UNC's national lab works through harm reduction organizations rather than individuals. Nowhere in about half of the country has anything.

national.name: UNC Street Drug Analysis Lab
national.access: Ask a local syringe service program or harm reduction org to submit for you; the lab offers free kits to any US public health harm reduction organization. Free for NC organizations and drug user unions.
national.anon: The lab states it holds nothing about individuals: no names, nothing.

national.name: Transparency Testing
national.access: Send a sample yourself, no organization needed. Around $40 to identify what something is, more for purity. They do not currently take liquids.
national.anon: They offer anonymous payment and state they delete customer data a month after results are sent.

national.name: Rebel Analytics (Rebel Harm Reduction)
national.access: Free, community-funded testing (FTIR, immunoassay strips, reagents, lab-partner mass spec). Their site describes a mail option for people outside NYC but does not publish which states, turnaround, or intake rules - contact them before sending anything.
national.anon: Anonymity policy not published on their site - ask them directly.
national.caveat: Details verified only as far as their own pages state them, 2026-08-10.

national.name: DrugsData (Erowid)
national.access: Not accepting samples since April 2024 (DEA order); no change expected before 2027, per their homepage. The archive of past results remains searchable and useful.

national.name: NEXT Distro
national.access: Mail-based naloxone and fentanyl test strips - strips are self-testing, not lab checking. Availability varies by state law.

programs.name: Berkeley NEED
programs.access: Free and anonymous, Thursdays 6 to 7pm only, first come first served. The navy van parks next to the white one near University and San Pablo.

programs.name: IE Safe Supply
programs.access: Kits on request, run with UC Riverside. Nothing identifying is collected and they state they do not work with law enforcement.

programs.name: Drug Checking Los Angeles
programs.access: Free, anonymous and legal, run by UCLA. Drop in at partner sites in Hollywood, South LA, East LA and downtown for a reading in minutes, or send a sample by post. Anything unclear goes to a lab at no cost.

programs.name: East Bay Drug Checking (HEPPAC)
programs.access: Readings on HEPPAC's sites and mobile unit around Fruitvale, Deep East Oakland and West Oakland.

programs.name: SCOPE - SF AIDS Foundation
programs.access: Free, anonymous, drop-in FTIR. 117 6th St (Mon 3-6, Tue-Wed 12-6) and 558 Clayton St (Fri 5:30-7:15). About 10-15 minutes; one sample per person per day. Call/text 415-361-8183.

programs.name: Connecticut Harm Reduction Alliance
programs.access: Free and confidential at two Hartford sites and one in New Haven. Reads fentanyl, xylazine, cutting agents and newer additives.

programs.name: CDPH community drug checking
programs.access: Runs through partner orgs; no public site list exists. Free test strips at CDPH clinics, or email osu.cdph@cityofchicago.org.

programs.name: Chicago Recovery Alliance
programs.access: Readings on the outreach van at six of its stops, and test strips at all of them. They will also test used packaging and cookers.

programs.name: AHOPE
programs.access: Walk in weekdays 7.30am to 3pm at 774 Albany Street, or find the mobile van. Checks for fentanyl and xylazine.
programs.caveat: The city describes this service in a news update rather than on a service page, so check the hours by phone before traveling.

programs.name: Tapestry Health
programs.access: Free, confidential and walk-in across Springfield, Holyoke, Northampton, Greenfield, Chicopee and Westfield, plus a mobile clinic.

programs.name: MADDS / StreetCheck
programs.access: Free through partner orgs in ~19 communities; anonymous option. Accepts powders, rocks, pills, single-use pipes/cookers/cottons, baggies with residue. Not syringes or plant matter.

programs.name: Rapid Analysis of Drugs (RAD)
programs.access: Through Maryland SSPs only - residue swabs from used equipment, deidentified. Ask your SSP.

programs.name: Check It
programs.access: A Johns Hopkins van that visits rotating Baltimore neighborhoods, with results in minutes alongside wound care and telemedicine. The schedule is linked from the page.

programs.name: Project DHARMA
programs.access: Reach it through Maine Access Points, commonspace or Portland Public Health. Readings on the spot, with harder samples confirmed by a lab.

programs.name: Grand Rapids Red Project
programs.access: Point-of-care readings, the first in Michigan, plus fentanyl, xylazine and medetomidine strips. Call ahead for current hours.

programs.name: Harm Reduction Michigan
programs.access: Lab analysis through their sites in Traverse City, Cadillac, Petoskey, Manistee and Midland. Each sample's report is published.

programs.name: Red Door Clinic
programs.access: Drug checking during syringe service hours at 525 Portland Avenue, four days a week. Call or text 612-596-9005 to confirm.

programs.name: Project EAGLE FANG
programs.access: St. Louis County public health with the SSM SLUCare toxicology lab. Tests both drug products and used equipment, and publishes every sample.
programs.anon: Samples go in anonymously - no age, no gender, nothing about who submitted them.
programs.caveat: The county states results are for research only and cannot be used in medical, legal or forensic matters. The page does not say where to hand a sample in; the contact address on it is the way to ask.

programs.name: NC Safer Syringe Initiative directory
programs.access: Drug checking reaches individuals through SSPs; the UNC lab is free in-state.

programs.name: Adulterant Checking Program
programs.access: The state health department runs this at four sites - Espanola, Albuquerque, Roswell and Las Cruces. A reading on the spot, and harder samples posted to a university lab, with results in about two weeks against an anonymous code.

programs.name: Southern Nevada Health District
programs.access: Clients of their harm reduction services can hand in used equipment or residue for analysis. What it finds feeds a public dashboard.

programs.name: NYS DOH drug user health FAQ
programs.access: Statewide pointers beyond NYC.

programs.name: New York State drug checking sites
programs.access: The state lists every participating site with its address - the Bronx, Albany, Schenectady, Buffalo, Jamestown, Rochester, Ithaca, Glens Falls, Long Island and more. Two kinds of testing: a reading on the spot, and a wipe test that finds traces.

programs.name: OnPoint NYC
programs.access: East Harlem and Washington Heights, open to 11pm on weekdays. Reads fentanyl, benzodiazepines, xylazine, ketamine and meth, with a partner lab for confirmation.

programs.name: NYC Health drug checking at SSPs
programs.access: Walk-in with a trained technician (FTIR + strips). Powders and pills; plant matter and most liquids cannot be tested. Call ahead to confirm.

programs.name: ACR Health
programs.access: Walk-ins welcome in Syracuse, Utica and Watertown. A reading on the spot plus fentanyl and xylazine strips.

programs.name: HIV Alliance
programs.access: Fridays 10am to noon on City View Street, and Wednesdays noon to 4pm at the Lavender Network. Listed by Lane County public health.

programs.name: White Bird Clinic
programs.access: 647 Polk Street, most days 9am to 5pm. Lane County lists it as a place to get drugs checked; their own page confirms fentanyl and xylazine strips in every kit.

programs.name: PA Groundhogs
programs.access: Free test kits posted anywhere in Pennsylvania, going out every Friday. Lab results in three to five days against an anonymous code, and they state they keep no data on the people who use it.

programs.name: Savage Sisters Recovery
programs.access: Runs an ongoing checking program to track what is in the local supply, with free naloxone and strips at every training.

programs.name: Rhode Island drug checking (RIDOH)
programs.access: Free, anonymous. Phone/text 401-473-9286 or 401-408-6451, weekdays 9-5.

programs.name: Harm Reduction Innovation Lab
programs.access: A Brown University pilot inside Rhode Island harm reduction sites - a reading on the spot, strips, and lab confirmation. The page gives a phone number rather than drop-in hours.

programs.name: Vermont community drug checking
programs.access: Legal statewide since 2023; availability varies by site - ask your syringe service program.

programs.name: Vermont CARES
programs.access: Free, anonymous and walk-in at Burlington, Rutland, Barre and St Johnsbury, with mobile days and delivery to around 29 towns.

programs.name: AIDS Project of Southern Vermont
programs.access: Walk in four days a week at 15 Grove Street; mobile visits around Bellows Falls and Bennington by appointment.

programs.name: WA Community Drug Checking Network
programs.access: Anonymous; drug or residue in a pipe or cooker. Not every site is listed - ask a local harm reduction agency.

programs.name: Tacoma Needle Exchange
programs.access: Free checking during Tuesday and Friday office pickup hours at 3716 Pacific Avenue. Call or text first to confirm.

locators.name: Harm Reduction Near You (National Harm Reduction Coalition)

legality.text: Whether test strips and checking equipment are legal depends on your state, and mailing samples touches state paraphernalia law - no program publishes a blanket promise that mailing is legal. Two maps track the actual laws:

sources.name: LAPPA state map - fentanyl test strips
Network for Public Health Law - drug checking equipment legality

grassroots.note: Peer-run and mutual-aid networks. Many operate primarily on social media - linked here as profiles, never embedded: an Instagram embed would hand Meta the IP of everyone opening this page.

orgs.name: Grassroots Harm Reduction
orgs.scope: National buyers’ club supplying local programs
orgs.access: Open to any organization or program that gives harm reduction supplies away free. Not a direct supplier to individuals — it is how the program near you affords what it hands out, and where to start if you want to run one.

orgs.name: Rebel Harm Reduction
orgs.scope: NYC community drug checking and supplies (see national list)
